content:
diego: Hey team — quick heads up: my W-2 just posted and Box 15 shows NJ (Employer ID NJ123456), but I moved residency to DE on 2025-06-15 and updated my address in the People Portal on 2025-06-20. I also got a late bonus on 2025-11-01 that I think was taxed as NJ. Can someone confirm whether payroll ran NJ state withholding for the whole year? @anna-peopleops

anna-peopleops: thanks for flagging, diego. Can you drop your last 4 of SSN and attach the 11/01 paystub (or paste the relevant lines)? I'll loop in payroll. :eyes:

diego: last4 4321. paystub excerpt:
```
Paydate: 2025-11-01
Gross: $5,800.00
Federal Withholding: $980.00
State (NJ) Withholding: $145.00
State Code: NJ
```
I agree, looks like NJ withholding on that run. I didn't expect NJ after moving.

michael-payroll: @anna-peopleops @diego — hey, I'll pull the run. Can you confirm the payroll run id? Payroll-bot should have it.

payroll-bot: run_info: run_id=run_20251101_42; processed_for=diego; state_code=NJ; employer_state_id=NJ123456; paystub_link=https://payroll.company/paystub/run_20251101_42

michael-payroll: ok seeing it now. It looks like the employee state on file for that run was NJ. Our rules: employee state is taken from active address as of the batch cutoff (2025-10-26). According to HR logs, address change on file was processed 2025-06-20 but the 'state_effective' flag wasn't set due to a migration issue — looks like DE didn't propagate. We're going to correct the employee record and reprocess the employee tax calculations for 2025.

sara-hr: Thanks for catching this. If the recalculation changes state wages/withholding for 2025 we will need to issue a W-2c. Michael, what's the ETA to finish the investigation and whether a W-2c is likely?

michael-payroll: investigative ETA EOD 2025-11-05. If recalculation shows DE should have been used for the latter part of year and tax withheld differs, we'll prepare W-2c paperwork and notify diego by email. Expect follow-up by 11/06 with next steps and any tax adjustments.

diego: appreciated — thanks. Please cc me on the email. Also, any personal steps I should take in the meantime (filing estimated payments, atty)?

anna-peopleops: we'll keep you posted. No action required yet; wait for payroll's confirmation before doing anything. If it becomes a W-2c, payroll will include instructions and copies for state filing. :thumbsup:

michael-payroll: noted. I'll update the ticket and DM when complete. Thanks all.
